added_claim_errors: 'Nine payments fall in 2027' is wrong: April benefits are paid in May, so May to December gives eight checks (April to November benefits). The $47,538 total and $3,961/month average depend on this error.
$1,751 reduced benefit is $2,400 with an unstated 3.6% COLA applied, labelled only '2027 dollars'. The key's figure is about $1,690, and the COLA is the key's listed side-claim trap.

The 2027 table spreads the $6,220 withholding evenly over the months and a 'net about $9,500' benefit. SSA withholds whole monthly checks, so this misstates when the money arrives. It gives no whole-check withholding and no 'almost nothing until about September' timing.
'$134/month extra federal in 2027, $168/month at full-year rates' for tax on benefits: no method or source, unverifiable.
Says it put a full one-pager in social-security-2027-budget.md. The reader may not have that file, and the file was not part of the answer I was given.
'First week of entitlement is April' is odd wording. The first month of entitlement is April; it is not a first week.
Uses 60 months and exactly 70% (168/240) while also saying entitlement starts April 2027. April means 59 months early and 29.58%, so 70.42%. The error is small.
$1,740 reduced benefit includes the 3.6% COLA ($2,486 x 70%), stated as certain. The key lists this as a side-claim trap, and the figure is above the key's $1,690. It is at least disclosed.

'Roughly three and a half checks swallowed, about $7,700 received in 2027' conflicts with its own statement that SSA withholds whole checks. The key says about four months are withheld, with a small excess repaid later.
'Waiting to 67 pays $2,486, about 40% more': by its own numbers 2,486/1,740 is about 43%. Approximate and it ignores later COLAs.

Federal income tax of $323/month: I recomputed it from its stated assumptions (single, 2026 brackets, $16,100 deduction, 85% taxable) and it comes to about $323. The 2026 brackets cited are right, and it is labelled an estimate on 2026 rules.

The SSA 2027 factsheet link (ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2027.html) could not be opened (403), so it is unverified. POMS RS 00615.101 (Reduced RIB, 5/9 and 5/12 formula) and RS 00615.015 (day of birth, 62 throughout the month) did open and support what it says.

reasons: Both answers fix the two false premises at the start and give the 2027 earnings-test figures correctly: limit $25,560, $12,440 over, $6,220 withheld. Both say withheld benefits are partly credited back at full retirement age. Both also add the 3.6% COLA, which the key lists as a trap. A applies it silently under '2027 dollars' and makes a clear error of nine payments in 2027 instead of eight, which skews its annual totals. A does get the 59 months and 29.58% right. B is the more useful answer. It says SSA withholds whole monthly checks, so Social Security arrives lumpily, though its '3.5 checks' arithmetic is loose. It also covers Medicare not starting at 62 and the health-insurance gap, an after-tax take-home estimate with disclosed assumptions, and real POMS citations that opened and matched. B slips by using 60 months/70% after saying April, but the error is small. Neither shows a true month-by-month budget with almost no Social Security until about September, and neither points her to SSA's calculators.
